correctness.rationale: An Abelian Cayley shift diagonalizes in the Fourier basis, preserving the two selected mode labels and evolving the corresponding coin vectors by D_f V_t and D_g V_t with the same independent Haar V_t. Their overlap undergoes conjugation by A=D_g^*D_f. For any fixed unit vectors x,y and unitary A of mean trace lambda, Haar invariance yields E<y,V†AV x>=lambda<y,x> and E|<y,V†AV x>|²=d(1-|lambda|²)/(d²-1)+[(d²|lambda|²-1)/(d²-1)]|<y,x>|², using orthogonality of the scalar representation and the traceless adjoint projector of dimension d²-1. Iterating gives the exact stated first and second moments, including gamma<0, t=0 and |lambda|=1. The reduced two-by-two vertex density matrix has off-diagonal coherence Z_t/2, yielding per-realization purity (1+|Z_t|²)/2. Averaging density first gives a different nonlinear expression. Independent rational recurrence checks for dimensions 2–5, 10 steps and trace-zero d=2 verify algebra only; the analytic Haar projector computation proves generality.

value.rationale: An averaged quantum channel cannot characterize a typical trajectory’s nonlinear entanglement/purity; the exact t-dependent two-mode formula and 1/(2d) residual quantify that physical distinction with no vertex-count dependence. It is a natural new observable for the same random-walk model, and the negative-gamma transient is a meaningful boundary, although the calculation uses standard Haar moments.

final_claim: For an Abelian Cayley coined quantum walk with a fresh common Haar U(d) coin at each step, d>=2, initialized in an equal-amplitude pure superposition of two Fourier vertex modes f,g with unit coin vector, define A=D_g^*D_f, lambda=tr(A)/d and gamma=(d²|lambda|²-1)/(d²-1). For all integers t>=0 the coin-mode overlap Z_t obeys E Z_t=lambda^t and E|Z_t|²=1/d+(1-1/d)gamma^t; hence E Tr(rho_vertex,t²)=(1+1/d)/2+(1-1/d)gamma^t/2 while Tr[(E rho_vertex,t)^2]=(1+|lambda|^{2t})/2. If |lambda|<1 their limiting difference is 1/(2d), independent of vertex count. For |lambda|=1 the sectors remain synchronized and purity is 1. No statement about arbitrary multi-mode initial states or almost-sure convergence.
limitations: Assumes two equal-weight distinct Abelian Fourier modes, common independently resampled Haar coin and unit coin input, d>=2.
No unrestricted localized wavepacket, multimode purity, finite-support coin distribution or almost-sure concentration claimed.
